questions.stem: Which is an example of a variable cost for a company that runs its workloads on AWS?

options.text: Buying servers for a company-owned data center
options.rationale: Purchased hardware is a fixed, up-front cost.

options.text: Signing a multi-year lease for a data center building
options.rationale: A building lease is a fixed cost.

options.text: Paying for Amazon EC2 instances for the hours they run
options.rationale: On-Demand compute is billed for the time it runs, so the cost varies with use.

options.text: Purchasing network switches months before they are needed
options.rationale: Up-front equipment purchases are fixed costs.

questions.explanation: In the cloud, costs move from fixed up-front investments to variable charges based on usage.

questions.stem: Which cost of running workloads on premises does a company stop paying for directly after moving those workloads to AWS?

options.text: Data transfer out to the internet
options.rationale: Data transfer out is still charged on AWS.

options.text: Licenses for software it brings to AWS
options.rationale: Bring Your Own License software still needs licenses.

options.text: Staff time to design and build its own applications
options.rationale: Designing and building applications remains the company's work.

options.text: Power and cooling for its own data center
options.rationale: AWS runs the facilities, so the company no longer pays for its own power and cooling.

questions.explanation: On-premises cost components include hardware, facilities, power, cooling and the staff to operate them. On AWS these are part of the service price.

questions.stem: A company has existing software licenses that it wants to use on Amazon EC2. What is this licensing approach called?

options.text: License included
options.rationale: License included means the license cost is part of the AWS price.

options.text: An AWS Marketplace software subscription
options.rationale: Buying through AWS Marketplace gets new software; it does not reuse licenses the company already owns.

options.text: Bring Your Own License (BYOL)
options.rationale: BYOL lets you use eligible licenses you already own on AWS.

options.text: Reserved Instance pricing
options.rationale: Reserved Instances are a compute pricing commitment, not a licensing approach.

questions.explanation: The clue is licenses the company already owns, which is BYOL. License included, the nearest alternative, means paying for the license through the AWS price.

questions.stem: Which statement describes a license-included Amazon EC2 instance?

options.text: The customer must buy the license from the vendor separately
options.rationale: That describes Bring Your Own License.

options.text: The software license cost is part of the instance price
options.rationale: With license included, AWS bills the license as part of the instance usage.

options.text: The software can be used without any license at all
options.rationale: The license still exists; it is paid through AWS.

options.text: The license requires the instance to run on a Dedicated Host
options.rationale: License-included instances run on shared tenancy too.

questions.explanation: License included is convenient when you have no existing licenses; BYOL can lower costs when you already own eligible licenses.

questions.stem: What does rightsizing mean in the AWS Cloud?

options.text: Running every workload on the largest available instance type to be safe
options.rationale: Oversizing wastes money; rightsizing does the opposite.

options.text: Buying Reserved Instances for every workload
options.rationale: Reserved Instances are a pricing choice; rightsizing is about resource size.

options.text: Matching instance types and sizes to workload needs at the lowest cost
options.rationale: Rightsizing selects the cheapest resource that still meets performance and capacity requirements.

options.text: Deleting all unused AWS accounts each month
options.rationale: Account cleanup is not what rightsizing means.

questions.explanation: Rightsizing is an ongoing process of matching resources to actual usage, and it is one of the main ways to lower AWS costs.

questions.stem: How does AWS CloudFormation help a company reduce operational costs?

options.text: It lowers the hourly price of every Amazon EC2 instance it launches
options.rationale: CloudFormation does not change resource prices.

options.text: It removes the need to monitor any resources
options.rationale: Monitoring is still needed; that is Amazon CloudWatch's job.

options.text: It provides free storage for all backups
options.rationale: CloudFormation is not a backup or storage service.

options.text: It automates provisioning from reusable templates
options.rationale: Infrastructure as code creates the same environment repeatedly without manual steps.

questions.explanation: Automation such as CloudFormation reduces the time and errors of manual provisioning, which lowers operating cost.

questions.stem: How can a managed database service such as Amazon RDS lower total cost of ownership compared with running the same database on Amazon EC2?

options.text: AWS performs routine tasks such as patching and backups
options.rationale: Managed services take routine administration off the customer's team.

options.text: Managed database services have no usage charges
options.rationale: Managed services are billed; savings come from less operational work.

options.text: It removes the need to pay for database storage and backup storage
options.rationale: Storage is still charged.

options.text: It lets customers skip controlling access to their data
options.rationale: Access control stays the customer's responsibility.

questions.explanation: Managed services such as Amazon RDS, Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS and Amazon DynamoDB reduce the undifferentiated work a team must do.

questions.stem: Which AWS service is a fully managed container orchestration service, so a company does not install and operate its own orchestration software?

options.text: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR)
options.rationale: Amazon ECR stores container images; it does not run or orchestrate containers.

options.text: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
options.rationale: Amazon EBS provides block storage volumes.

options.text: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)
options.rationale: Amazon ECS is a fully managed container orchestration service.

options.text: Amazon EC2
options.rationale: Amazon EC2 provides virtual servers; orchestration on EC2 means installing and operating the software yourself.

questions.explanation: The clue is container orchestration without running your own software, which is Amazon ECS. Amazon ECR, the nearest neighbor, stores the container images that ECS runs.

questions.stem: A company's internal application is used only during business hours. How can the company lower its AWS costs for this workload?

options.text: Buy extra on-premises servers as a standby
options.rationale: Extra hardware adds fixed cost.

options.text: Run the largest instances around the clock
options.rationale: Oversized, always-on resources raise cost.

options.text: Stop or scale in resources outside business hours
options.rationale: Turning off idle capacity means you stop paying for it.

options.text: Deploy additional copies of the workload in more AWS Regions
options.rationale: More copies add cost without reducing idle time.

questions.explanation: Paying only for what you use means scheduling resources to match usage is a direct saving.

questions.stem: Which TWO are benefits of using AWS managed services instead of self-managed software on Amazon EC2? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Full administrator access to the underlying host operating system
options.rationale: Managed services do not give access to the host operating system.

options.text: Built-in options for scaling and high availability
options.rationale: Managed services offer features such as Multi-AZ deployments and automatic scaling.

options.text: No charges for using the service
options.rationale: Managed services are billed.

options.text: Less time spent on routine maintenance such as patching
options.rationale: AWS performs routine administration for managed services.

options.text: No responsibility for controlling access to data
options.rationale: Access control remains with the customer.

questions.explanation: Managed services shift operational work to AWS while the customer keeps control of data and access.

questions.stem: Moving workloads from a company data center to AWS typically shifts spending from what to what?

options.text: From operating expenditure to capital expenditure
options.rationale: This reverses the shift.

options.text: From variable costs to fixed costs
options.rationale: The cloud turns fixed costs into variable ones.

options.text: From capital expenditure to operating expenditure
options.rationale: Up-front hardware purchases are replaced by ongoing pay-as-you-go charges.

options.text: From software licensing to up-front hardware purchases
options.rationale: Cloud adoption reduces hardware purchases.

questions.explanation: Trading fixed (capital) expense for variable (operating) expense is a core economic benefit.

questions.stem: Which service helps a company manage its software licenses from vendors such as Microsoft and Oracle across AWS and on premises?

options.text: AWS Artifact
options.rationale: Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements.

options.text: AWS License Manager
options.rationale: License Manager tracks license use across AWS and on premises and can enforce licensing rules.

options.text: AWS Cost and Usage Reports
options.rationale: Cost and Usage Reports give detailed billing data; they do not track license use or enforce license rules.

options.text: AWS Service Catalog
options.rationale: Service Catalog offers a catalog of approved IT products that users can launch; it does not track license counts.

questions.explanation: The clue is managing software licenses from vendors, including ones brought under BYOL. License Manager tracks license use and enforces limits, while Service Catalog controls which products users can launch.

questions.stem: Which service analyzes utilization and recommends better-sized Amazon EC2 instances to reduce cost?

options.text: AWS Compute Optimizer
options.rationale: Compute Optimizer uses utilization data to recommend optimal resource sizes.

options.text: AWS Pricing Calculator
options.rationale: Pricing Calculator estimates costs before you build.

options.text: AWS Budgets
options.rationale: Budgets alerts on spending thresholds.

options.text: AWS Artifact
options.rationale: Artifact provides compliance reports.

questions.explanation: Compute Optimizer supports rightsizing, one of the most effective cost practices.

questions.stem: Which is a fixed cost for a company running its own data center?

options.text: Paying per GB-month for Amazon S3 storage
options.rationale: S3 storage is a variable, usage-based cost.

options.text: Buying servers sized for peak demand
options.rationale: Hardware bought up front costs the same whether it is used or idle.

options.text: Per-second billing for Amazon EC2 instances
options.rationale: Per-second billing is variable.

options.text: Per-request charges for AWS Lambda
options.rationale: Lambda requests are a variable cost.

questions.explanation: On premises, capacity for peak demand is paid for even when it sits idle.

questions.stem: Which TWO costs belong in a total cost of ownership comparison between an on-premises data center and AWS? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: A fee for each sign-in to the AWS Management Console
options.rationale: The console has no separate charge.

options.text: Server hardware and data center facilities
options.rationale: Hardware and facilities are major on-premises costs.

options.text: A monthly subscription fee for Basic Support
options.rationale: Basic Support is included for all AWS customers.

options.text: Staff time spent operating the infrastructure
options.rationale: Operations labor is part of total cost of ownership.

options.text: A charge for creating each new AWS account
options.rationale: Creating an AWS account has no charge; you pay for the resources you use.

questions.explanation: A fair comparison includes everything it takes to run on premises: hardware, facilities, power, cooling, networking, licensing and the people who run it all. The other options are charges that AWS does not make.
